facts.text: Alvarado’s historic district preserves the town’s roots in Mexican land grants, especially the Potrero de los Cerritos grant that once covered almost all of Alvarado.
Anthony Gualco, a lifelong history buff, gathered more than 1,500 pages of Alvarado stories, newspapers, and photographs for the town’s online archive.
The online archive, hosted at https://alvarado-history.wdgeo.com, was organized and uploaded by Diane’s husband in 2022, making the town’s past easily accessible.
Gualco’s research also documents the histories of nearby towns that were annexed, such as Centerville and Decoto, adding context to Alvarado’s development.
The historic district’s buildings reflect the era when Alvarado was a small farming community, with architecture that dates back to the late 1800s.
Alvarado’s name honors its founder, Anthony, whose birth town is highlighted in the district’s extensive chapter collection.
